name: Shemaiah
overview: Shemaiah was a male Levite known for his role in distributing portions to his brothers, a responsibility that highlights his service within the tribe of Levi. His actions are recorded in 2 Chronicles 31:15, underscoring his involvement in the organization of Levitical duties. There are no additional notes that expand upon his character beyond this service.
namesAndTitles: The name Shemaiah means 'YHWH hears,' which reflects a theologically significant meaning common to Hebrew proper names. This name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries the implication of divine attentiveness. The meaning aligns with the spiritual context of his Levitical role.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Shemaiah as a son of Levi, situating him firmly within the Levitical lineage. Beyond this tribal affiliation and his role in distributing portions, no other family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shemaiah's significance lies in his practical service to the Levitical community, particularly in managing the distribution of portions to his fellow Levites. This task was critical for maintaining the order and provision among those dedicated to temple service. His mention in 2 Chronicles 31:15 highlights the importance of faithful stewardship in God's appointed roles within Israel.
